name: heat_pump_nh3_two_stage_flooded
title: Two-stage NH3 heat pump with flooded evaporator (TESPy benchmark vs Ebsilon)
summary: Two-stage ammonia heat pump (condenser, valve, drum with circulation pump and flooded evaporator, vapour superheater, two compressors with intercooler) heating water from 60 to 105 C: design point plus an off-design point with characteristic lines, after the TESPy heat-pump benchmark with an Ebsilon COP matrix.
language_features: arrays for the diagram state points

authors: Francesco Witte (TESPy lead developer) and the TESPy contributors
origin.notes: COP reference values of an Ebsilon model are the arrays of the test file; the Ebsilon model itself is not available. TSP-038 (stepwise NH3 tutorial) is a duplicate of this physics. Translation published under the CoolSolve_Library MIT licence (decision D3).

verification.summary: The TESPy test was re-run (CoolProp 8.0.0): CoolSolve agrees with all stored states, powers, duties, UA and COP at the design and 90 C/25 kg/s points (157 variables, max 4.0e-7, pumps) and with the COP of all 20 off-design points to 2.0e-9. Versus the Ebsilon COP matrix: -5.6 % to +6.3 %.
verification.reference: TESPy tests/test_models/test_heat_pump_model.py (commit 19425523) re-run in a throw-away venv (TESPy 0.11.3.dev0, CoolProp 8.0.0): design point and 20 off-design points; Ebsilon COP matrix of the test (4 sink temperatures x 5 source flows)
verification.notes: compare_solution.py --rtol 1e-6 on design + baseline (157 common variables, 0 differ, max 4.03e-07 W_dot_pu_o; states and COP <= 2.7e-9). 20-point sweep: COP <= 2.0e-9 vs TESPy; vs Ebsilon max |deviation| 6.25 % at 90 C / 10 kg/s (test tolerance 7 %).
